archetypes.name: flag-removal-completeness
archetypes.rationale: --convergence-threshold is removed from run-step3-review.sh callers, but plan-review-loop.sh itself (not in the diff) may still parse or require the flag — a silent mismatch would cause argv-validation failures at runtime.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the removal of `--convergence-threshold` from `run-step3-review.sh` and all call sites in the diff is complete and consistent with `plan-review-loop.sh`, which is NOT changed in the diff. Specifically: does `plan-review-loop.sh` still have a `--convergence-threshold` case in its argv parser? If yes, passing the flag would cause an unknown-option error; if no, the removal is clean. Also check `docs/configuration-and-permissions.md` (the `LARCH_DESIGN_CONVERGENCE_THRESHOLD` section is removed in the diff — confirm the contrast note at the end of `LARCH_DESIGN_ROUND_CAP` no longer references the removed var), `skills/design/references/plan-review.md`, and any other harness or doc file that the diff does not touch but that might still reference `LARCH_DESIGN_CONVERGENCE_THRESHOLD` or `--convergence-threshold`. Confirm the new `test-design-structure.sh` `absent` assertions (lines 241-242 in the diff) would catch any surviving references in SKILL.md and run-step3-review.sh. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-stub-precision
archetypes.rationale: The new write_stub_enum_failure checks for -mindepth in argv — if should_remove_by_age also uses -mindepth, the stub would accidentally fail the nested-scan path and produce misleading test results.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine `write_stub_enum_failure` in `skills/cleanup/scripts/test-cleanup.sh` (added in the diff): it exits 2 when any argument equals `-mindepth`. Determine whether `should_remove_by_age` in `cleanup.sh` (the existing nested-activity scan that uses `-maxdepth 5`) also passes a `-mindepth` argument to `find`; if it does, the enum-failure stub would inadvertently fail the nested scan during the `enumeration-failure-warns` and `enumeration-failure-warns-tmp` test cases, which would cause those cases to both warn AND skip the nested-scan protection check — masking real behavior differences between enum-failure and scan-failure. Also verify that the `mktemp-allocation-failure-warns` test case (which uses `chmod 000` on TMPDIR) correctly reverts permissions with `chmod 755` before `unset TMPDIR` regardless of script exit, and that `CACHE_REMOVED` and `TMP_REMOVED` KVs are actually present in output when mktemp fails (the spec says cleanup still emits removal-count KVs). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
